name: Ursula Bechtolsheimer-Kipp
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2018-2020); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Ursula Bechtolsheimer-Kipp is the daughter of Karl-Heinz Kipp, deceased founder of the Massa department store chain.
The family fortune began with 500 bottles of rare wine that her father sold on the post-war black market.
Karl-Heinz Kipp sold the Massa chain in 1985, but smartly held on to the underlying property and struck a lucrative lease deal with retailer Metro.
His legacy includes the Tschuggen Hotel Group, a Swiss luxury resort group; Ursula took over as chairwoman in 2016.
Top-rated properties include the Tschuggen Grand Hotel in Arosa, Hotel Eden Roc in Ascona and the all-suite Carlton Hotel in St. Moritz.
forbes_facts: Ursula is married to horse breeder Wilfried Bechtolsheimer, with whom she runs a horse farm in Gloucestershire, England.
Their daughter is dressage rider and Olympic gold medallist Laura Tomlinson. One of their three sons is a member of Gothic band Curse of Lono.

name: Maurizio Billi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Maurizio Billi is president of Eurofarma, a Brazil-based pharmaceutical firm that sells generic versions of drugs such as Viagra.
Eurofarma was founded by his father in 1972 and became one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in Brazil, with more than $1.8 billion in revenues.
Eurofarma expanded to Central and South America by acquiring medical suppliers, labs, and other pharmaceutical companies.
The company has operations in 22 countries and employs more than 12,600 people.
forbes_facts: Maurizio Billi is an avid car racer. Several times his Eurofarma team has won the Brazil circuit of Stock Car Brasil, the Brazilian equivalent of Nascar.

name: Antonio Del Valle Ruiz
name_chinese: 安东尼奥·戴尔·瓦莱·鲁伊斯
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Antonio del Valle Ruiz swapped a stake in a Mexican bank for control of what is now chemical conglomerate Orbia Advance Corp.
He and his six children own a 46% stake in Orbia Advance Corp., formerly called Mexichem.
Del Valle also owns a majority stake in Grupo Financiero BX+, which controls the bank Banco Ve Por Mas.
Through the family's Grupo Kaluz conglomerate, the Del Valle's also own stakes in construction companies Elementia and Fortaleza Materiales as well as Chicago's Byline Bank.
Del Valle has put his children in executive positions at his companies, but is still involved in strategic decisions as "Honorary Chairman for Life."

name: William Hockey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: In 2012, William Hockey cofounded payments company Plaid, which helps other fintechs connect to customers' bank accounts.
He met his cofounder Zach Perret while they were both working as junior consultants at Bain & Company.
He stepped down as Plaid's chief technology officer in 2019, but he remains a board member.

In 2022, he launched Column, a chartered bank based in San Francisco that helps other businesses (including Mercury and Brex) offer banking services. Hockey self-funded Column and owns the vast majority of it.
Hockey studied history and business at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

name: Laura Love
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Laura Love and her three siblings own Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, a truck stop and convenience store chains with over 600 locations in 42 states.
Her parents, Tom and Judy Love, founded the company in 1964 using a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents.
Brothers Frank and Greg Love are co-CEOs of the $22 billion (est. sales) company.
Sister Jenny Love Meyers is chief culture officer and EVP.

name: Bang Si-hyuk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Bang Si-hyuk is the founder and chairman of Hybe (formerly Big Hit Entertainment), one of Korea's largest music labels and entertainment agencies.
He took the company public in 2020 in what was South Korea's largest IPO in three years, which made him a billionaire.
Hybe's success is attributed to its seven-member boy band, BTS, which scored six No. 1 albums on the U.S. Billboard 200.
Bang worked as a composer for JYP Entertainment, one of Korea's "Big Three" music agencies, before venturing out on his own.
In 2021, Hybe acquired Ithaca Holdings, which manages Justin Bieber and Ariana Grande, for over $1 billion.

name: David Booth
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: When David Booth cofounded Dimensional Fund Advisors in 1981, he began a decades-long experiment in applying academic theory to real-world investing.
His former professor Eugene Fama authored the efficient markets hypothesis, which argues that it's impossible to consistently beat the market.
In light of Fama's research, Booth eschewed stock picking and focused on offering investors low-cost, passive mutual funds.
Dimensional manages $777 billion in assets, most of which is steered via hand-vetted financial advisors.
Booth joined the Giving Pledge in 2018, committing to donate at least half of his wealth to charity.
forbes_facts: Booth paid $4.3 million for James Naismith's original rules of basketball, written in 1891, which is now displayed at the University of Kansas.
In 2008, Booth donated $300 million to the University of Chicago, which is still the largest gift in its history.

name: Xu Jinfu
sec_insider_companies: Jinxin Technology Holding Co (NAMI) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Xu chairs Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology, a supplier of chemicals to sectors such as lithium-ion battery and personal care.
The company has 20 sites in China, Europe and the U.S., and is eyeing new plants in Texas and Morocco.
Xu obtained a bachelor's degree from Zhejiang University and a master's from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, both in chemistry.

name: Zhixiang Zhang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2008-2009)
forbes_bio: Zhang Zhixiang is the chairman of privately held Jianlong Group, one of China's largest non-government controlled steelmakers.
The company is also involved in the shipbuilding and mining industries.
Jianlong was ranked no. 53 on a list of China's 500 largest private companies in 2018.

name: David Adelman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: David Adelman is a real estate, alternative investments and sports mogul.
His Campus Apartments is one of the largest providers of on- and off-campus housing in America, with some $2 billion of properties across 80 schools in 23 states.
He is also cofounded Future Standard, an alternative investments firm that manages $86 billion across mutual funds, REITs and other vehicles. He's vice chairman.
He has a 7% stake in Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment, which owns the NHL's New Jersey Devils and the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers. He's spearheading a plan to build the Sixers a $1.3 billion arena.
A Philadelphia native, Adelman got his start using $2,000 of bar mitzvah money to invest with student housing entrepreneur and family friend Alan Horwitz.
He then went to work for Horwitz, rising to CEO at age 25, and began taking more and more of the equity as he expanded Campus Apartments nationwide.
forbes_facts: Adelman first invested in a building at the corner of 45th and Pine streets, which he still owns today. He chose it at age 13 because it was the tallest one he saw.
Through his Darco Capital, Adelman has invested in everything from soccer club Crystal Palace F.C. to private jet charter company WheelsUp, where he's on the board.

name: Zhang Jin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Zhang Jin chairs Guangdong-headquartered Cedar Holdings, whose business interests include real estate, finance and auto sales.
Born the son of a government worker, Zhang first prospered from stock investments.
Zhang Jin is a graduate of Shenzhen University.

name: Heikki Kyostila
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Heikki Kyostila is president of Planmeca, one of the world's largest dental equipment manufacturers, headquartered in Helsinki, Finland.
Kyostila founded Planmeca in 1971 in Helsinki as a small dental-stools and -cabinets manufacturer.
The company has expanded to making  2D and 3D imaging X-ray devices and software for dentists.
forbes_facts: Kyostila was the on the cover of the first edition of FORBES Finland, in April 2017.

name: Benjamin Otto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Benjamin Otto inherited a 15.1% stake in Otto Group, which his grandfather, Werner, started as a mail-order business in 1949.
His father, Michael Otto, he ran the business for 26 years until 2007. He is now chairman of its supervisory board.
With revenues exceeding $15 billion, Otto Group has more than 40 companies in retail (including Crate and Barrel), real estate and financial services.
Benjamin joined the family company as an executive director in 2012.
forbes_facts: Benjamin Otto and his wife are active in philanthropic organizations focused on healing through alternative treatment methods.

name: Richard Fortin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Richard Fortin is a cofounder and board member of Alimentation Couche-Tard, a Canadian convenience store giant that owns the Circle K chain.
Couche-Tard does $73 billion in annual revenue across more than 17,000 stores.
Fortin, a golf and fishing enthusiast, also owns stakes in the National Bank of Canada and Canadian packaging and publishing company Transcontinental.
His Fondation Lise et Richard Fortin supports causes like assistance for the elderly and services for children who are survivors of sexual assault.
The chain has made three other cofounders billionaires: former CEO Alain Bouchard, Jacques D'Amours and Réal Plourde.
